title: Methodology
subtitle: How we choose, report, check and correct what we publish.
body:
The Utah View publishes monthly briefings on global politics across five regions: the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa. This page explains how that work gets done, so you can judge it for yourself.

How we choose stories

We ask two questions about every story: how many people does it affect, and what is likely to happen next because of it. A story that matters a great deal but gets little coverage elsewhere often makes our list for exactly that reason. We don't choose stories for traffic, and we don't chase the 24-hour news cycle. A monthly schedule gives us time to wait for the facts.

Where our information comes from

  • Primary sources first. Wherever possible, we work from the original record: government statements and documents, court rulings, election results, official statistics and published data.
  • Reporting by others, credited. We are not on the ground in every country we cover. When we rely on reporting by another news organization, we name it and link to it.
  • Expert and academic work. For background and context, we draw on research from universities, think tanks and international bodies. We note where a source has a known point of view.
  • Claims are attributed. When a fact is disputed, we say who is making the claim instead of stating it as settled.

How we check facts

Before a piece is published, it is reviewed by one of our editors, the editors and admins The Utah View has invited to its newsroom. They check names, numbers, dates and quotes against the original source.

Briefings, analysis, opinion and data

Every story is labeled so you know what kind of piece you are reading.

  • Briefings report what happened in a region and why it matters. They don't argue for a side.
  • Analysis goes deeper on one issue. It explains causes and likely outcomes, and the evidence for them.
  • Opinion is the author's own argument, under their name. It does not speak for The Utah View.
  • Data pieces are built on a dataset. We name the dataset, link to it where it is public, and explain how we used it.

Independence

The Utah View is independent and reader-supported. Advertisers and algorithms have no say in what we cover or how we cover it.

Writers and editors don't cover people, companies or organizations they have a personal, family or financial tie to. If a writer has a relevant connection, they tell an editor first. The editor then either assigns someone else or adds a note about it at the end of the piece. We don't accept payment, gifts or free travel in exchange for coverage.

Corrections

If we get something wrong, we fix it. A correction note at the end of the story says what changed and when. We don't quietly edit errors away. To report an error, use the “Spot an error? Tell us” link at the end of any story. Every report goes straight to our editors.

Questions

If something on this page doesn't match what you see in our coverage, we want to hear about it. Write to us through our Contact page.
